== Enshrined deities ==
'''Main deity'''
* '''{{ill|Tachibanahime-no-Mikoto|ja|弟橘媛|ko|오토타치바나히메|zh|弟橘媛|qid=Q11487396|lt=Ototachibana-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' (おとたちばなひめのみこと)

'''Co-enshrined deities'''
* {{ill|Yamato Takeru|arz|ياماتو تاكيرو|be|Ямата Такэру|de|Yamatotakeru|es|Yamato Takeru|fa|یاماتو تاکه‌رو|fr|Yamato Takeru|hu|Jamatotakeru|id|Yamato Takeru|it|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|ko|야마토타케루|pt|Yamato Takeru|ru|Ямато Такэру|sh|Yamato Takeru|simple|Yamato Takeru|sq|Jamato Takeru|sr|Јамато Такеру|sv|Yamato Takeru|tr|Yamato Takeru|uk|Ямато Такеру|ur|یاماتو تاکیرو|vi|Yamato Takeru|zh|日本武尊|zh_min_nan|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} (やまとたけるのみこと) - husband of Ototachibana-hime.
* Oshiyama no Sukune (おしやまのすくね) - father of Ototachibana-hime.

== History ==
== Overview ==
Shrine tradition says that during Yamato Takeru's eastern campaign, when crossing from {{ill|Sagami Province|ckb|پارێزگای ساگامی|cs|Provincie Sagami|de|Provinz Sagami|es|Provincia de Sagami|fa|ولایت ساگامی|fr|Province de Sagami|gl|Provincia de Sagami|id|Provinsi Sagami|it|Sagami (provincia)|ja|相模国|ko|사가미국|lt|Sagamio žemė|nl|Sagami (provincie)|pt|Província de Sagami|ru|Сагами (провинция)|simple|Sagami Province|sk|Sagami (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сагами|tr|Sagami (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Саґамі|zh|相模國|zh_min_nan|Sagami-kok|zh_yue|相模國|qid=Q1053732|lt=Sagami}} to Kazusa and encountering a storm at sea, his consort {{ill|Tachibanahime-no-Mikoto|ja|弟橘媛|ko|오토타치바나히메|zh|弟橘媛|qid=Q11487396}} sacrificed herself to calm the seas. Yamato Takeru then made her tomb, enshrined her comb, and planted tachibana trees; this is said to be the origin. The ''{{ill|Kojiki|ace|Kojiki|ar|كوجيكي|az|Kociki|bcl|Kojiki|be|Кодзікі|bg|Коджики|ca|Kojiki|ckb|کۆجیکی|cs|Kodžiki|da|Kojiki|de|Kojiki|eo|Koĝiki|es|Kojiki|et|Kojiki|eu|Kojiki|fa|کوجیکی|fi|Kojiki|fr|Kojiki|gl|Kojiki|he|קוג'יקי|hi|कोजिकी|hr|Kojiki|hu|Kodzsiki|hy|Կոձիկի|id|Kojiki|it|Kojiki|ja|古事記|ka|კოძიკი|kk|Кодзики|kn|ಕೋಜಿಕಿ|ko|고사기|la|Kojiki|lt|Kodžiki|mk|Коџики|ml|കൊജികി|ms|Kojiki|my|ခိုဂျိခိ|nl|Kojiki|no|Kojiki|oc|Kojiki|pl|Kojiki|pt|Kojiki|ro|Kojiki|rsk|Кодїки|ru|Кодзики|sh|Kojiki|simple|Kojiki|sk|Kodžiki|sl|Kodžiki|sr|Коџики|sv|Kojiki|ta|கோஜிகி|th|โคจิกิ|tl|Kojiki|tr|Kojiki|uk|Кодзікі|vi|Cổ sự ký|zh|古事記|zh_classical|古事記|qid=Q813031}}'' says "After seven days, her comb came ashore; they took it and made a tomb"<ref>[https://www.seisaku.bz/kojiki/kojiki_11.html Kojiki, Middle Book 4, Emperor Keiko]</ref>, and this is identified with this shrine. In the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}'', the related account of Yamato Takeru's sea crossing and onward route is also regarded as the origin narrative<ref>[https://www.seisaku.bz/nihonshoki/shoki_07.html Nihon Shoki, Vol.7, Emperor Keiko Chronicle]</ref>.

== Precinct ==

Behind the honden remains a {{ill|Kofun|ca|Kofun|cs|Kofun|da|Kofun|de|Kofun|eo|Kofun|es|Kofun|fa|کوفون|fi|Kofun|fr|Kofun|he|קופון (רוגם)|hr|Kofun (grobnica)|id|Kofun|it|Kofun|ja|古墳|ko|고훈|my|ခိုဖွန်း|pl|Kofun (kurhan)|pt|Kofun|ru|Кофун (захоронение)|simple|Kofun|th|โคฟุง|tr|Kofun|uk|Кофун|zh|古墳|qid=Q1141225}} said to be the tomb of Ototachibana-hime-no-Mikoto. Before the honden was built, worship is said to have been directed from the haiden straight toward this tumulus. The Miyazuma Pond in the precinct is traditionally said to be a pit from digging that tomb.

== Sessha and massha ==
[[ファイル:橘樹神社 (茂原市) 摂末社.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Sessha and massha]]
All are massha.
* Akiba Shrine
** Deities: Izanami-no-Mikoto, Homusubi-no-Mikoto
*: Invited in the Tensho era.
* Kasushima Shrine
** Deity: Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto
*: Invited in the Bunroku era.
* Inari Shrine
** Deity: Ukemochi-no-Mikoto
*: Enshrined since the foundation.
* Koyasu Shrine
** Deity: Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto
*: Invited in the Eiroku era.
* Kureto Shrine
** Deity: Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Mikoto
*: Relocated together with the fall of Honno Castle.

== Cultural properties ==
== Chiba Prefecture designated cultural property ==
* Tachibaki-sha documents (with petition and complaint documents of Hasegawa Arinori) (calligraphy) - designated March 10, 1989.

== Mobara City designated cultural properties ==
* Honno Tachibana Shrine grove (natural monument) - designated Feb 26, 1980.
* Miyanoshita ruins (historic site) - designated Dec 28, 1978.
* Tachibana Shrine Ogiu Sorai calligraphy plaque (with Sorai's autograph "Koto no Ki") and sacred cedar (calligraphy) - designated Jan 22, 1993.
